(page title) Haze | Blur the profile they build on you
(description for search and link previews) Haze is a privacy app in design. It will add decoy activity built to behave like real people, test it against a detector, and show you the result. Join the waitlist.
Haze
Join the waitlist
In design. Not available yet.
Blur the profile they build on you.
Every search, visit and tap adds to a profile of you. Haze will add decoy activity built to behave like real people, so that profile says less about the real one.
Join the waitlist
See how it works
Illustrative model. Not measured performance.
Your activity makes a pattern.
When you are online. What you look at. How much, and how often. Put together, it is enough to guess your routine, your interests and a good deal more.
A VPN hides your traffic from your internet provider. A blocker stops some trackers. Neither changes the pattern you leave with the sites and apps you actually use.

Illustrative model. Not measured performance.
Haze would give them a crowd.
Haze will run decoys beside you. Each one has its own interests and its own daily rhythm, and none of them moves in step with you. A profile built on the mix is meant to be a blurrier picture of the real you.

Illustrative model. Not measured performance.
Tested decoys, not random noise.
Random noise can be told apart from real behavior and thrown away. So the plan is to test every kind of decoy against a detector built to catch fakes, and to keep only what passes.
Random
Tested
Caught
Passes
Detector
Illustrative model. Not measured performance.
You would see the result.
Haze will show a score: how easily a detector can pick your real activity out of the mix. If it can still pick you out, you will see that.
Haze
Sample screen

The blur is not working.
Illustrative model. Not measured performance.
Ground rules.
It will run on your device. Your real activity will stay there.
No fake ad clicks. That costs other people money.
Decoys will stick to ordinary, everyday content.
You will set the limits: data, battery and hours.
What it will not do.
It will not make you anonymous.
It will not change what a service learns while you are signed in to it.
It is not a VPN or an ad blocker. It will work beside them.
We do not know yet how much it will help. Finding out is the point of building it, and we will publish what we measure.
Should we build it?
Haze is not built yet. The decoy engine and the detector exist in our lab. The app does not. Join the list and tell us two things. If enough people want it, we build it, and you hear first.

Join the waitlist
The list holds your email, these answers and the day you joined. Nothing else. One email when there is news. To leave the list, email hello@whoffagents.com.
Haze is a working name from Whoff Agents.
This page loads nothing from other companies and sets no cookies. The hosts that serve this page and take your signup keep ordinary request logs, which include your IP address. Those logs do not hold your email or your answers.
(described to screen readers) Illustration. A profile made of points of activity loses its sharp edge as other points drift through it.
(described to screen readers) Illustration. Scattered points of activity gather into rows across a day, and a profile of routine and interests comes into focus.
(described to screen readers) Illustration. Decoy activity appears beside the real activity, each row with its own timing, and the profile under it goes soft.
(described to screen readers) Illustration. Random decoys are caught at a detector and dropped. Tested decoys pass through it.
(described to screen readers) Illustration of a sample screen. A marker on a gauge moves between easy to pick out and hard to pick out.
